Swiss Army Bench 0.0.8: projects in one .sab file, and a Start page.

- **Projects as one .sab file:** a project's notebooks, scripts and app canvases, its grids with their steps, the
  Sandbox, the relationships and the window layout, in one file you can email or keep on OneDrive. Opening it puts
  everything back: each table is read again from where it came from (a connection by name, a file, a notebook, a
  query) and its steps are applied.
- **Rows only when you tick them:** a pasted or pushed table has no source, so Save as offers "Keep its rows in the
  file" for each one, off by default. No password, token or secret is ever written into a .sab; connections go in
  by name.
- **When a table can't come back** (a connection this computer doesn't have, a file that moved), a strip under the
  tabs offers the fix: Add connection, Find the file, Try again, or Remove.
- **The Start page:** New project, Open project…, your recent projects (a missing one is marked, with Remove from the
  list), and your recent notebooks and scripts. It shows when nothing is open, and the mark (Home) brings it back.
- **Save, Save as… and Close** sit at the top of the page with the project's name; ● means unsaved, and Ctrl+S saves.
  The Workbench follows the project too, and a folder project can be saved as a .sab.
- **Open from anywhere:** `swissarmybench open file.sab`, and on Windows a double-click on a .sab opens it (the
  installer registers the file type for you, no admin needed). On Linux the installer adds the file type; macOS
  isn't registered yet.
- **The agent can do it too:** open, save, save as, close, the recent list and a table's fix. It asks your Allow
  only when a save would write rows into the file.

Update from the tray (right-click, Update to 0.0.8), then run the installer once more so a double-click on a .sab
opens it:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/DylanCodyBrown/SwissArmyBench/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```
